gfi_title: Marketplace exchange platform for ingredients, inputs, & services
scope_note: Ingredient sourcing for human food
vietnam_evidence: Buyers already meet sellers through distributors (Brenntag, VMC, TDGIMEX), the Food Ingredients Vietnam fair (about 250 exhibitors, May 2026) and the HoReCa platform Kamereo. The commodity exchange MXV has 33 members and links to CME Group and others under Decree 302/2026/ND-CP, but food-grade defatted soy flour is not exchange-traded.
verdict_note: Covered by the delivered-price sheet for soy flour and textured soy (DMV-21) and the public price series (P6). A platform adds little where buyers meet sellers through distributors and fairs. Hedging the soybean element of flour cost through an MXV member is a component to test, not a finding.
signal_to_watch: Food-grade soy flour or textured soy quoted on a Vietnamese B2B platform or exchange

gfi_title: Developing rigorous demand forecasts
scope_note: Market-size forecasts are out of scope; demand is sized only as labelled scenarios
vietnam_evidence: The study's demand scenarios and open demand model already do the permitted part.
verdict_note: Rule: no market-size forecasts; published market sizes without a traceable method are not findings.

gfi_title: A toolkit for B2B sales resources and training
scope_note: Business-to-business selling of protein ingredients
vietnam_evidence: Large processors import major ingredients directly and expect in-person contact; small firms buy 20 to 25 kg bags from distributors (section 16.5). No Vietnamese training or toolkit for ingredient sales found; none searched for specifically.
verdict_note: The standing panel of 10 to 15 research and procurement buyers (DMV-08) and the buyer map (D5) do this job for Vietnam.

gfi_title: Pooled procurement/group purchasing for ingredients and inputs
scope_note: Joint buying of soy flour or textured protein by food makers
vietnam_evidence: Law on Competition 2018 bans outright agreements fixing prices of goods among firms in the same relevant market (Art. 11(1), 12(1)); exemption possible (Art. 14). Law on Cooperatives 2023 lets 5 or more members, including Vietnamese legal persons, form a cooperative that serves members through internal transactions, with tax relief and preferential credit (Art. 4, 22, 23, 30). No chay makers' association or joint-buying group found; FFA-HCMC became a business association in November 2025 with no joint buying described.
verdict_note: T1 and section 26.7: adds a constraint and a vehicle. Pooled buying or pooled offtake should be parallel bilateral contracts with the line owner, or a cooperative of 5 or more members; an agreement among competing chay makers on the price they pay carries legal risk (our reading, not legal advice).
signal_to_watch: A chay makers' cooperative or association that buys soy flour or textured protein jointly

gfi_title: Coordination among investors with alternative protein industry-specific expertise
scope_note: Investor coalitions, syndication, debt and inventory finance
vietnam_evidence: No disclosed institutional round for any Vietnam-based alternative-protein company; no disclosed Vietnamese deal above USD 5 million (S11.1). VPCA exists as a general investor network. Debt and inventory finance exist as bank products (see GFI-060).
verdict_note: There is no Vietnamese deal flow for an investor coalition to syndicate. The debt and inventory-finance part is handled under GFI-060.
signal_to_watch: A Vietnam-based alternative-protein company raising a priced round above USD 5 million

gfi_title: Guaranteed offtake contracts for products and ingredients
scope_note: Offtake agreements to make a first plant bankable
vietnam_evidence: T1 kill test already requires 3 buyers with conditional orders of 2,000 t a year. Banks finance suppliers against anchor buyers: BIDV offers up to 85% of order value to SMEs referred by an anchor company. IFC says suppliers are typically paid 30 to 60 days after delivery. Public meals buy through caterers, not the state (section 15.3). No regional precedent of a PE lead, DFI ticket and buyer offtake (S11.6).
verdict_note: T1: an offtake from a large anchor buyer (CJ Foods Vietnam, Vissan, a national distributor) is also what unlocks bank supply-chain finance for the line's receivables. Adds a test: will the anchor's bank include the T1 supplier in its supply-chain programme.
signal_to_watch: A named Vietnamese food maker signing a conditional supply contract or letter of intent for domestic textured protein

gfi_title: Dedicated broker or exchange for plant-based B2B sales
scope_note: Selling plant protein to frozen and prepared-food makers
vietnam_evidence: Ingredient distributors (Brenntag, VMC, TDGIMEX) already sell plant proteins to small makers; chay makers, co-packers and frozen-food makers are T1's named first customers.
verdict_note: The distributor route and named first customers in T1 cover the broker function.

vietnam_evidence: Appendix D4 maps retail, foodservice, institutions and tourism channels; D5 and buyer_map.csv name business buyers.
verdict_note: D4 and D5 already serve as the Vietnamese directory; DMV-08 adds contact with buyers.

gfi_title: Establishing intellectual property pooling frameworks
scope_note: Sharing patents among firms
vietnam_evidence: T1 has no intellectual property (ch26); fermentation plays would license strains and processes from abroad. We did not search patent databases.
verdict_note: No Vietnamese holders of alternative-protein patents to pool.
signal_to_watch: A regional patent pool or pledge open to ASEAN firms, or Vietnamese-held patents in food fermentation

gfi_title: Platform for facilitating matchmaking between funders and funding-seekers
scope_note: Matching funders with researchers and startups
vietnam_evidence: The package lists grants, funds and their 2026 status (S11.10, funding_programs.csv) and research funding (S7.10).
verdict_note: Covered by S11.10 and funding_programs.csv; the research-funding database is screened by line L6 (GFI-015).

gfi_title: Infrastructure loan fund
scope_note: Loans and guarantees for first plants
vietnam_evidence: Existing state instruments not in the package: SME Development Fund lending to value-chain and cluster SMEs (Decree 45/2024/ND-CP); HCMC SME Credit Guarantee Fund (new charter 29 May 2026: up to 100% of a loan, about VND 34 billion or USD 1.3 million per customer for investment loans, 20% owner's equity); Decree 57/2018/ND-CP processing support of 60% of investment up to VND 15 billion per project if value rises at least 1.5 times (replacement draft at 30%, March 2026). NATIF and Decree 156/2025 already in the package.
verdict_note: RM-12: a T1-scale line (USD 0.28 to 1.38 million installed) can already use SME guarantees, SMEDF loans and Decree 57/2018 support, so the concessional window is needed for T4 and T5 scale, not T1.
signal_to_watch: Issue of the decree replacing Decree 57/2018; any guarantee or SMEDF loan to a food-protein processor
source_ids: GSD-01; SLK-10; SLK-20; SLK-21; SLK-22; SLK-23

gfi_title: Infrastructure and equipment leasing fund
scope_note: Leasing equipment for a processing line
vietnam_evidence: Circular 26/2024/TT-NHNN (in force 1 July 2024) allows finance leases and sale and leaseback of machinery and production lines, in VND unless the lessee earns foreign currency. Eight leasing companies operate; production lines were over VND 6,900 billion of leases at 30 June 2025; BSL says over 40% of its book is production machinery, mainly for SMEs. A January 2026 draft would raise the small-value threshold to VND 400 million. Lessors' terms not read (sites unreachable).
verdict_note: T1: the extruder, dryer and packing line can be financed by a finance lease or sale and leaseback from a licensed lessor. Leasing does not cover working capital, which is T1's larger need.
signal_to_watch: A lessor quoting terms for an imported food-extrusion line
source_ids: GSD-01; SLK-01; SLK-02; SLK-03; SLK-04; SLK-24

gfi_title: Investor conference for LPs, funds of funds, corporate VCs, family offices, and money managers
scope_note: Investor conference for alternative protein
verdict_note: A conference needs companies raising money; Vietnam has none in these families yet. Vietnamese firms can use regional events.
signal_to_watch: A Vietnam-based alternative-protein company raising a priced round

gfi_title: Options for factoring financing for alternative proteins
scope_note: Factoring and supply-chain finance for working capital
vietnam_evidence: Circular 20/2024/TT-NHNN (in force 1 July 2024, replaced Circular 02/2017) allows factoring with and without recourse and factoring for the purchaser, under one year, in VND; SBV circulated a draft amendment in March 2026. Factoring balances about VND 16,000 billion (about 0.1% of credit) in August 2025. BIDV offers supplier finance, buyer-side and seller-side factoring and distributor overdrafts across nearly 100 supply chains (SCFast 2026, up to VND 15,000 billion). IFC and SECO support a supply-chain finance programme to 2029.
verdict_note: T1: names the 'trade finance' in the T1 advice. The line's receivables from an anchor buyer can be factored or financed as supplier finance; distributors can carry stock on overdrafts. Works only with an anchor the bank already finances, which reinforces ownership by or contract to a large chay maker, co-packer or distributor.
signal_to_watch: Issue of the amended factoring circular; a food or chay anchor added to a bank supply-chain programme
source_ids: GSD-01; SLK-05; SLK-06; SLK-07; SLK-18; SLK-19

gfi_title: Expanding alternative protein accelerator programs
scope_note: Accelerators
vietnam_evidence: 2026 programmes in HCMC: Green Innovation Accelerator (sustainable agriculture track, revenue of at least USD 1 million, benefits worth nearly USD 20,000) and the AHTP high-tech agriculture startup contest (agricultural processing in scope). No food-protein or alternative-protein track found. Regional specialists already listed (S11.11).
verdict_note: S11.11 covers accelerators; the two 2026 programmes update it and partly answer OQ-070 for HCMC.
signal_to_watch: An alternative-protein or food-ingredient track at a Vietnamese accelerator, NIC or SIHUB

gfi_title: Expanding corporate investment capabilities within strategic industry partners
scope_note: Corporate venture arms of food groups
vietnam_evidence: No corporate venture arm of a Vietnamese food or dairy group found (Masan, Vinamilk, TH, Nutifood, KIDO, PAN). VinVentures (Vingroup, USD 150 million, 2024) targets AI, semiconductors and cloud. Vinh Hoan's 2021 stakes abroad are in the package. CPF is tagged on Kamereo's 2021 round (paywalled).
verdict_note: Vietnamese food groups act through their balance sheets (joint ventures, supply contracts, acquisitions), not venture funds. The likeliest lead for a first plant remains a domestic strategic buyer (S11.6).
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese food or dairy group launching a venture arm or startup programme with a food-ingredient focus

gfi_title: Facilitating import and export of alternative protein products
scope_note: Export facilitation for food made in Vietnam
vietnam_evidence: Under the 2026 National Trade Promotion Programme, MOIT ran a Vietnam pavilion of about 16 booths at the Private Label Show (Chicago area, 15 to 17 November 2026); the state paid 100% of booth rent and standard build. Rules-of-origin guidance is already DMV-19.
verdict_note: DMV-11: the state-funded pavilion at private-label fairs is a ready venue for the importer-quote test of a plant-protein or protein-upgraded chay product. No new play.
